- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and model overestimates, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- After a recent spike (sentiment = 1.00), model tends to overreact; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and model is consistently high, apply downward bias correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast.
- Avoid forecasting >10% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strong (≥0.75) — otherwise, model overestimates volatility.
